goal: Adds a new RPC, getnetmsgstats, exposing global per-message network traffic broken down by direction, network, connection type, and message type.
Lets node operators and monitoring tools see exactly how bandwidth is spent across peer types and message kinds, beyond what per-peer getpeerinfo/getnettotals offer.

result.summary: This PR adds a new RPC, getnetmsgstats, that reports cumulative network traffic (bytes and message counts) broken down by direction, peer network, connection type, and message type, aggregated globally in CConnman rather than per-peer. It introduces a NetStats class storing atomic counters in a 4D array, hooks it into CNode::ReceiveMsgBytes and CConnman::SocketSendData, and adds a functional test exercising the new RPC's output format and behavior under partial message reads.
result.problem: Per-peer traffic stats (bytessent_per_msg etc.) are lost once a peer disconnects, so operators cannot get a global, historical breakdown of bandwidth by network, connection type, or message type. Node operators with capped or metered bandwidth want to know where their traffic goes; this is tracked in issue #26337 and has had two prior PR attempts.

The category file explicitly places 'RPCs that merely report peer state' outside p2p, and here the net.cpp/h changes exist solely to serve that reporting purpose.
categories.rationale: Not a p2p behavior change; the net.cpp instrumentation is mechanical support for the new RPC and has no effect on protocol correctness, attack resistance, or relay, so it is excluded per the category's own carve-out for reporting-only RPC support code.

result.card: Adds a new RPC, getnetmsgstats, that exposes global (not per-peer) network traffic broken down by direction, peer network, connection type, and message type, implemented via a new NetStats class hooked into CNode::ReceiveMsgBytes and CConnman::SocketSendData. It solves a real gap for node operators who want historical bandwidth breakdowns that survive peer disconnects, tracked in issue #26337 and attempted twice before (#27534, #28926); a production user, waketraindev, reports already using it in a node-monitoring dashboard. Review has been substantive over two years, with concept ACKs from epiccurious, danielabrozzoni, and stickies-v, and the one real design objection (an RPC-side aggregation option) was resolved when the author removed that feature in June 2026. The PR currently needs a rebase and the author has gone quiet for months despite repeated pings from sedited, so it is not reviewable as-is. No open PR dependencies; earlier overlap with #29421 was resolved by merge and rebase.
